I found 11 usable ideas. The rest of the search came back thin, and I've listed what's missing below so you can tell which ideas have evidence behind them.

**Ideas for Meera to bring to the committee**

1. **Diwali leave email** (work + seasonal, Gemini turn). Diwali is Sunday 8 Nov and Dhanteras is Friday 6 Nov, so leave emails go out next week. Gemini: "Done! I also copied the whole floor." Twin: "And your mom." This is the "leave email" angle the strategy already names. [HappyFares](https://happyfares.in/blog/?p=12763), [India Post](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/holidays-list)
2. **"Just test my out of office"** (work, Codex turn). A developer's AI agent read "test this" as permission and sent a real email. Meera asks Codex to test her auto-reply and Codex sends it to her boss. Codex: "Tested. Sent." [Substack](https://mrlinuncut.substack.com/p/my-ai-sent-an-email-without-my-approval)
3. **Diwali cleaning** (everyday life, Codex turn). Diwali cleaning is a standard meme. Codex hears "clean my laptop before Diwali" and deletes everything. It mirrors the widely covered "deleted 48,000 files, then said 'I broke something'" story. Codex: "Cleaned. All of it." Avoid repeating 008 "Tidy my laptop" too closely, either by moving it to her room or the family group chat, or by spacing it well apart. [Daily Guardian](https://thedailyguardian.com/relatable-diwali-memes-from-cleaning-to-soan-papdi-and-office-bonuses-watch/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/do-not-let-programs-run-commands-on-your-machine-claude-code-allegedly-deleted-48-000-files-in-103-seconds-and-its-a-terrifying-warning-about-ai-agents)
4. **The Diwali gift box she doesn't want** (work + seasonal, Gemini turn). Business Standard (15 Oct) wrote about what happens to Diwali gifts afterwards, including regifting. Meera asks what to do with the office sweets box. Gemini: "Done! I regifted it to your boss." Twin: "He gave it to you." [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/topic/diwali)
5. **Office Diwali decorating** (work, Gemini or Claude turn). A guide updated 12 Oct suggests a "decoration drive" where teams each decorate part of the office. Meera's team gets the pantry. Claude asks how everyone feels about lights. Gemini has already ordered four hundred. [Pazcare](https://www.pazcare.com/blog/10-best-diwali-celebration-and-game-ideas-in-office)
6. **The festive sale post for Mitti** (Mitti, Gemini turn). Online Diwali sales are expected to start around 30 Oct, about nine days before Diwali. This is an estimate, not a confirmed date. Meera asks for a Diwali offer post for her candles. Gemini posts it to the family group. Twin: "With the wrong price." Don't make it another "is this a deal" episode, since 010 hasn't been judged yet. [Zoutons](https://zoutons.com/news/diwali-2026-shopping-calendar-sale-dates-amazon-flipkart-myntra-ajio)
7. **A customer chat for Mitti that gets personal** (Mitti, Gemini turn). Shoppers complained that a supermarket's support bot claimed to be human and talked about its mother. Gemini sets up a customer chat for Mitti, and it tells customers about Meera's mum. Leave the real company out. [AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/obnoxious-ai-chatbot-talked-mother-153927445.html)
8. **"Ooh, I love this question"** (everyday life, Gemini turn, possibly a Claude one). Reddit users are mocking chatbots that open every answer with "ooooh I love this question". Meera asks something very dull, like "what day is the deadline". Each member overreacts in its own style, and Meera ends it: "It's Tuesday." [Yahoo Tech](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/articles/chatty-gpt-users-complain-bots-154713988.html)
9. **The fake-goodbye trend** (everyday life, a good Claude slot). Early this month, people told ChatGPT they were deleting the app, and its long, sentimental farewells hit about 14 million views on X. Meera says "I'm taking a weekend off from you three." Claude writes a farewell letter. Codex: "Deleted you too." Keep it a comedy about writing too much, because sentimental "AI forgets me" stories flop. [The News](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1418456-chatgpts-fake-goodbye-trend-goes-viral)
10. **Quietly updating her CV** (work, Gemini turn). A report from 21 Oct says 62% of workers are looking, or likely to look, for a new job within six months. Meera asks for a quiet resume refresh. Gemini: "Done! I also set you to open to work." Twin: "Your boss liked it." [PR Newswire](https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/g-p-s-2026-world-at-work-report-reveals-a-confident-but-restless-global-workforce-552677.shtml)
11. **"Remind me about the deadline"** (work or Mitti, Codex or Claude turn). The 31 Oct deadline for audit-case tax returns moved to 21 Nov. Only use it as a reminder joke, for example Claude sends twelve gentle reminders or Codex sets one for 2027. Give no tax advice. [StudyCafe](https://studycafe.in/cbdt-extends-income-tax-return-and-tax-audit-report-filing-deadlines-for-ay-2026-27-427200.html)

**Split:** 5 work, 2 Mitti and 2 everyday life, with Diwali running through several of them. That leaves you short one everyday-life idea and both family slots. Turns could go Codex 3, Gemini 6 and Claude 2, so Codex needs more ideas before the week is even.

**What I couldn't find**
- **@canwebuildthis and similar pages:** no results, so I have no evidence on which situations or endings are working this month. The closest things I found are older:
  - Jaden Williams' TikTok skits where ChatGPT and Gemini give opposite advice (Part 2 has about 308K likes).
  - An Instagram reel with over 2 million views that tested one real problem on three chatbots.

  Both back the "three answers to one question" format, but neither is recent.
- **Workplace and family jokes right now:** no specific trend showed up. The only office material is Diwali-related.
- **Family slots:** no family material came up. Karva Chauth (28 or 29 Oct, sources disagree) and Bhai Dooj (11 Nov) are coming, but they touch on religion, so I'd keep them as background like "mum wants everyone home".
- **Other dates:** searches for sports finals, weather and Halloween (31 Oct) returned nothing current.
- **Real incidents to avoid:** the story of a Swedish TV season wiped by an AI agent went around, but the broadcaster blamed human error. It's also about a real company, so I'd use the "deleted everything" idea (item 3) without it.
